passage:
A university built a digital model of a city to test traffic plans. On the screen, cars, buses, bikes, and pedestrians moved through virtual streets.
Students watched engineers test what would happen if one road became bus-only. The model predicted less traffic in one area but more in another.
The engineer explained that a digital model is useful, but it is not the real city. People may behave differently from predictions.
The students learned that planning needs both simulation and observation.
A digital twin can help people imagine consequences before building. But the real city still has weather, habits, emotions, and surprises.
